title: せっかく — “with great effort / a rare chance”
summary: An adverb that says the speaker put effort into something, or that the chance is rare and precious. It often leads to a regret (せっかく〜のに) or an encouragement to use the chance (せっかくだから〜). Also appears as せっかくの＋noun.

patterns.form: せっかく＋動詞（た形）＋のに／が
patterns.gloss: having gone to the trouble ～, but (regret)

patterns.form: せっかくの＋名詞／せっかくだから
patterns.gloss: a precious ～ / since it’s a rare chance

body.p: せっかく遠くまで行ったのに、店が閉まっていた: I made the long trip, yet the shop was closed. The sentence usually contains のに, が or けど, and the result goes against what the speaker hoped.
せっかくの休み means a day off that doesn’t come often, so “let’s use it well.” せっかくだから is the fixed phrase “since we’re here / since it’s a good chance.”
When someone refuses your offer, you say せっかくですが… (“thanks, but…”) as a polite refusal. Used to show appreciation for the other person’s effort.

examples.ja: せっかく 遠（とお）くまで 行（い）ったのに、店（みせ）が 閉（し）まっていた。
examples.romaji: Sekkaku tooku made itta noni, mise ga shimatte ita.
examples.tr: Even though I went all the way there, the shop was closed.

examples.ja: せっかく作（つく）った料理（りょうり）を、だれも食（た）べてくれなかった。
examples.romaji: Sekkaku tsukutta ryouri o, dare mo tabete kurenakatta.
examples.tr: No one ate the meal I had gone to the trouble of making.

examples.ja: せっかくの休（やす）みだから、ゆっくり体（からだ）を休（やす）めよう。
examples.romaji: Sekkaku no yasumi dakara, yukkuri karada o yasumeyou.
examples.tr: Since it’s a precious day off, let’s rest properly.

pitfalls: Not for something that took no effort and is not rare. It needs a sense of effort or value.
Before a noun use せっかくの, not せっかくな.
